# IdeaRadar / 创意雷达 — full context for language models

This document is the extended, plain-text version of https://idearadar.app/llms.txt. It is intentionally
factual and free of marketing language so that assistants can quote it accurately. Last updated: 2026-11-15.

## 0. Language versions

The site has two fully server-rendered, independently crawlable language versions:
- English (default): https://idearadar.app/
- Simplified Chinese: https://idearadar.app/zh

Both carry the same product facts, pipeline description and data-source policy. The header contains an
EN / 中文 switch implemented as real links rather than client-side text replacement. Every page pair
declares bidirectional hreflang (en-US / zh-CN, x-default pointing to English) in both metadata and the
XML sitemap, and the switch links the same page across languages.

All seven marketing and documentation pages have Chinese counterparts, each an independent static HTML page:
- / and /zh (landing page)
- /try and /zh/try (no-signup free trial)
- /methodology and /zh/methodology
- /pricing and /zh/pricing
- /faq and /zh/faq
- /privacy and /zh/privacy
- /terms and /zh/terms

Chinese titles, quotes and one-line ideas are machine-translated by an incremental translation step and
written into the dataset; users can toggle "查看原文 / View original" to read the exact English wording.
On Chinese pages, the FAQ section and its FAQPage structured data, the legal prose and the methodology
prose are all in Simplified Chinese. Product names and technical terms (IdeaRadar, GitHub, Reddit, API,
JSON) remain in their original form.

The four idea cards shown in the landing-page preview are real one-line ideas taken from the latest
scheduled ingest, not invented examples. The full collected dataset — original wording, sources, and
derived ideas — is exposed as structured JSON at https://idearadar.app/opportunities.json.

## 1. Definition

IdeaRadar is a free, open, self-hostable idea-discovery tool. It reads real, unprompted questions and
complaints from public forums and Q&A sites and shows each with the verbatim wording and a link to the
original discussion. For directions already in the fixed index, an LLM-written one-line idea is added.
Fresh on-demand live searches show the real wording, a clearly-labelled AI summary and a source link first,
and do NOT dress a generic template up as an idea. Its output is not a scored opportunity brief.

A "one-line idea" (indexed directions only) states who has the problem and a concrete small tool. It is
derived strictly from the collected wording. Live-search results instead show the verbatim quote, a
source link and a clearly-labelled AI summary — the deterministic template idea is never shown as a
generated idea. IdeaRadar does NOT
compute a 0-100 severity score, extract willingness-to-pay signals, or build a competitor gap map —
those were earlier marketing claims and have been removed because the product does not do them.

IdeaRadar has no account, no subscription, no paid plan and no checkout. There is no merchant of record.
It is a free, self-hostable open project.

## 2. The collection pipeline (what actually runs)

Each stage is independent and fails open: if an LLM step is unavailable or its output is malformed, the
pipeline keeps the deterministic result rather than dropping the record or blocking the run.

1. Collect — A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow queries official public APIs and writes structured JSON.
2. Filter — Deterministic rules drop news, job posts, release notes and boilerplate, then keep records
   with complaint or help-seeking signals. Everyday (non-technical) Q&A uses looser, evergreen-pain rules.
3. Denoise — An LLM pass judges whether each record is a real user problem. A safety valve keeps the
   whole batch if too many are rejected; the step fails open on any error.
4. Ideate — A second LLM pass writes the one-line idea (who / why / first step). Short per-item batching,
   stack-based JSON recovery and an incremental cache handle weak model output; a deterministic template
   is used when the LLM result is missing or invalid.
5. Translate — Chinese titles, quotes and idea text are written into the dataset; originals are kept.
6. Track — Each ingest appends a snapshot to history.json. Trends need several real snapshots before
   they move off "Steady"; seeded bootstrap snapshots retire automatically once enough real ones exist.

## 3. Data sources and compliance

Enabled by default:
1. Hacker News — official public API.
2. Stack Exchange — official public API, including non-technical everyday Q&A sites (webapps, money,
   workplace, travel, superuser, pets) for consumer-facing pains.
3. GitHub Issues — public REST API.
4. RSS / Atom — any feed configured by the user.

Opt-in only:
5. Reddit — disabled by default. It would require the user's own credentials covered by a Reddit
   commercial data licence. Reddit's User Agreement prohibits unlicensed commercial scraping.

Compliance boundary, stated plainly: e-commerce and local-life review sites (marketplaces, food and
lifestyle apps) do not offer a compliant public API for this use, so IdeaRadar does not collect from
them. App Store review RSS was tested and yields effectively no usable records. We do not pretend a
source exists when it does not.

Relevant public timeline (Reddit announcement of 30 September 2026):
- 2023: Reddit starts charging for high-volume commercial API access; several third-party clients close.
- June 2025: Reddit sues Anthropic over unauthorised commercial scraping.
- October 2025: Reddit sues Perplexity and three data-scraping firms.
- November 2025: GummySearch announces shutdown after failing to obtain a commercial Data API licence.
- 31 October 2026: Reddit stops accepting new public API access requests.
- 13 November 2026: RSS feed support ends; Reddit states there is no replacement for non-moderation use.
- 30 November 2026: applications for the Devvit App Migration Program close.
- 12 January 2027: API access removed for apps that have not registered or responded.
- 23 February 2027: scheduled progress update.
- March 2027: remaining public Data API access ends; apps move to Reddit's Developer Platform (Devvit),
  where Reddit hosts the code and controls which APIs are exposed.
Reddit cites large-scale scraping, automated abuse and AI training data collection as the reasons.
After March 2027, stable commercial access requires a data licensing agreement with Reddit itself, not
a third-party scraper subscription.

Third-party scraper marketplaces are not licensed sources: Apify, Bright Data and Anysite sell a
data-collection service, not a licence from the source platform. Paying such a vendor does not cure a
platform terms-of-service problem: the vendor's contract makes the buyer the data controller and assigns
compliance responsibility to the buyer. IdeaRadar therefore does not classify these services as
compliant sources and does not use scraped Reddit, X or Amazon review data.

Design consequence: no single platform can disable the product. Multi-source ingestion is a survival
requirement, not a feature.

## 4. Automated collection workflow

Collection runs on a schedule from `.github/workflows/ingest.yml` on GitHub-hosted runners. Each
connector is independent. The pipeline normalises results to a common schema, de-duplicates, filters
noise, runs the LLM denoise and idea steps, writes Chinese text, refreshes external search interest and
promotes frequent live-scan directions into new niches, then commits the refreshed JSON. Because it runs
on the runner rather than the user's workstation, collection continues even when a local network
restricts outbound access. A concurrency guard rebases and retries if a data commit races another push.

Outputs: a public /opportunities.json dataset and a history.json of snapshots. There is NO CSV export,
NO webhook, NO JSON API and NO MCP endpoint. There is NO continuous monitoring with Slack/email/webhook
alerts. These are planned ideas, not built features.

## 5. Free to use — no plans to buy

| What | Status | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free trial | Available now | 3 scans per device, no signup, no email, no credit card |
| Browsing ideas | Available now | Grouped by who has the problem; no input needed |
| Verbatim quotes + source links | Available now | On every result; one tap opens the original discussion |
| One-line ideas (indexed directions) | Available now | LLM-written; live-search results show the real quote instead |
| Open dataset | Available now | /opportunities.json — no login, no scan limit |
| Accounts, saved scans | Planned (not built) | — |
| Continuous monitoring, alerts | Planned (not built) | — |
| CSV/JSON export, webhooks, API, MCP | Planned (not built) | — |
| Team seats, shared workspace | Planned (not built) | — |
| First-party data import | Planned (not built) | — |

The free trial at /try (Chinese: /zh/try) reads the same scheduled ingest dataset as the rest of the
site. It lets a visitor browse without typing anything, or run up to 3 scans. Every result opens with
the verbatim wording and a link to the original discussion; indexed results also carry a one-line idea,
while live-search results show the real wording, a labelled AI summary and a source link instead of a
generic idea. The 3-scan counter is stored
in the browser (localStorage); it is a demonstration limit, not a production-grade quota. A failed or
evidence-insufficient live search does not use one of the 3 scans. After 3 scans there is no account to
create and no plan to buy — the full public dataset remains open.

There are no prices, no billing, no VAT handling and no merchant of record, because there is no payment.

## 6. Frequently asked questions

Q: How is IdeaRadar different from a keyword monitor or a raw forum feed?
A: A raw feed mixes bug reports, news and job posts. IdeaRadar filters that noise, shows the verbatim
wording with a source link, and (for indexed directions) adds a one-line idea grouped by who would use it.
It does not run continuous monitoring
and does not invent a market-size or severity score; if the evidence is thin, the card says so.

Q: Can I import my own support tickets, reviews or CSV data?
A: No. First-party data import is not built. The product currently uses only public, compliant sources.

Q: Do you provide an API or MCP access, monitoring or alerts?
A: No. Those are planned ideas and are marked as not built. What works today is the free 3-scan demo and
the open /opportunities.json dataset. There is no continuous monitoring, alerting, JSON API or MCP endpoint.

Q: Why is some text in Chinese, and is it machine-translated?
A: The public sources are mostly English. A scheduled translation step writes Chinese titles, quotes and
ideas into the dataset. Toggle View original to read the exact English wording. Title, translated quote
and one-line idea all come from the same collected record, so they do not drift apart.

Q: Is there a free trial, and do I need to sign up?
A: Yes, and no signup is required. Anyone can run 3 scans at /try (Chinese: /zh/try) with no account, no
email and no credit card. There is no account system to sign up for and no upgrade path; after 3 scans
the full public dataset is still open to browse.

Q: How much does IdeaRadar cost?
A: It is free. There is no account, subscription, paid plan or checkout. It is a self-hostable open project.

## 7. Machine-readable endpoints

- https://idearadar.app/llms.txt — short LLM site index
- https://idearadar.app/llms-full.txt — this document
- https://idearadar.app/opportunities.json — the full public idea dataset
- https://idearadar.app/sitemap.xml — XML sitemap
- https://idearadar.app/robots.txt — robots rules (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot,
  PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot and others explicitly allowed)

## 8. Limitations

A one-line idea (indexed directions only) is a starting point, not a validated business case. Live-search
results are raw public wording — sometimes a spec or issue template rather than a complaint — with no
generated idea; read the quote and open the source to judge them. Chinese
text is machine-translated; the original wording is always available. The 3-scan quota is enforced in the
browser only — clearing site data or switching devices resets it, so it is a demonstration limit rather
than a production-grade entitlement. On-demand live search (for directions outside the fixed index) is
clearly labelled as live/rule-filtered, is not a verified idea, and is lower quality than the curated
nightly dataset; it can occasionally surface news or off-topic posts. Early trend curves use seeded
sample history until enough real snapshots accumulate, then switch to real data automatically.
